items.title: Fatal Gua Musang crash survivor makes positive progress
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: A 21-year-old woman who was critically injured in a crash that claimed three lives along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai Road near Gua Sejuk yesterday is showing positive progress after being transferred to Sultan Ismail Petra Hospital (HSIP), Kuala Krai, for further treatment. Another victim killed was the Perodua Myvi driver, Muhamad Syazwan Hakimi Ibrahim, 21, while the trailer driver escaped unhurt. The remains of Nur Balqis' mother and younger brother were buried at the Kampung Melor Lama Muslim Cemetery, Kota Bharu, while Muhamad Syazwan Hakimi's remains were laid to rest at the Kampung Tegayong Muslim Cemetery, Melor, Kota Baru, this morning.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls close: Race for the state government begins
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The polls have officially closed across Negeri Sembilan. After two weeks of intense campaigning, voters have cast their ballots for all 36 state seats, leaving the state on a knife-edge as the race to form the next government begins. The unity government banner that saw Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN) sweep 31 seats three years ago has vanished, replaced by a fragmented and fierce contest.

items.title: Counting begins for nearly 12,000 postal ballots as Negeri Sembilan polls enter final stretch
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Postal vote counting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election began at 5pm today. Approximately 12,000 postal ballots are being counted. On 20 July, EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said a total of 13,263 postal ballots had been issued to eligible voters for the state election.

items.title: Merdeka Center: Pakatan’s eight-year track record could matter more than shifting alliances in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) ability to retain voter support in the Negeri Sembilan state election will hinge on whether its eight-year administration has convinced voters that its performance outweighs shifting political alliances. Merdeka Centre programme director Ibrahim Suffian said the state election would indicate whether voters continued to value governance and stability, given that PH has governed Negeri Sembilan since 2018 without any major administrative crises or controversies. While national political developments would inevitably shape voter sentiment, Ibrahim said the state government’s own track record would remain an important consideration at the ballot box.

items.title: NS polls: EC pilots digital voter attendance system at polling centre
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The diverse demographic profile of voters at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato Klana Petra Maamor near Ampangan made it the ideal location for the Election Commission's (EC) pilot Optical Character Recognition Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system during the Negri Sembilan election. The OCR-VA system was developed to record and verify voter attendance at polling streams by automatically scanning information on voters' identity cards. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the commission was using seven polling streams at the school for the pilot project, marking the first step towards digitalising voter attendance records.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan voter turnout climbs to 65.38pc by 4pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voter turnout in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election reached 65.38 per cent, with 562,133 of the 859,760 registered voters having cast their ballots as of 4 pm. The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, reported that the Kota state constituency recorded the highest turnout so far at 72.1 per cent, closely followed by Seri Menanti and Labu at 70.9 per cent each. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Sabah to secure 40pc stake in floating LNG project, says Hajiji
items.summary: KALABAKAN: Sabah is set to sign an agreement with Petronas that will see the state acquire a 40 per cent stake in a floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) project. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the milestone was made possible through a cooperation agreement previously signed with Petronas, enabling the state government to participate more actively in Sabah's oil and gas industry. He said Sabah continued to attract growing investor interest due to the state government's investor-friendly policies, a fact acknowledged by foreign diplomats who had visited the state to explore investment opportunities.

items.title: 20,000 Cambodians still unable to return home after Thai clashes: UN
items.summary: BANGKOK: More than 20,000 Cambodians remain displaced along the border with Thailand following last year's clashes, a UN expert said Friday, urging both sides to resolve the crisis. - STILL SCAMMING - Andrews concluded his first official visit to Cambodia on Friday, where he also raised concerns about the victims trafficked to work in scam centres, and wider restrictions on political rights. Andrews said he also pressed Cambodia's leaders to ensure everyone implicated in the scam centres faced justice, including high-level officials.

items.title: Tengku Permaisuri Selangor outraged over animal cruelty
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Hajah Norashikin, has expressed her profound sorrow, disappointment and anger over recurring acts of cruelty towards domestic pets and stray animals, particularly dogs and cats that continue to go viral. As the Royal Patron of the Stray Free Selangor (SFS) initiative under SPCA Selangor, Her Royal Highness said torturing, injuring, killing, or mistreating animals not only violates the law, but also reflects a failure to uphold basic human compassion and the fundamental values of a civilised society. She also urged the government, local authorities, relevant agencies, and the public to collaborate under the shared motto of "Compassion.

items.title: Mixing politics with business destroys parties, Sanusi warns PAS members against project‑seeking donors
items.summary: GERIK, Aug 1 — PAS has reminded its members to steer clear of business figures seeking to approach the party solely to secure projects without following proper procedures. PAS election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said such practices could damage the party’s internal ecosystem, especially when business entities began demanding projects and bypassing due process, Berita Harian (BH) reported today. When asked whether the Tabung Haji RCI findings might affect cooperation between Barisan Nasional and PAS, Sanusi said the matters raised in the report had no link to PAS.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 9 states, KL and Putrajaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nine states, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 7pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a weather warning issued at 3.45pm, said the affected areas in Perak are Manjung, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Mualim. On the east coast, the warning covers Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Baru, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, as well as Kuala Nerus, Hulu Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu, Marang, Dungun and Kemaman in Terengganu.

items.title: Stakeholder feedback crucial in Tabung Haji Act amendments, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1—Engagement sessions with stakeholders are currently underway to gather feedback on the proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535), as recommended by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the move aims to strengthen the legal framework and overall management of the pilgrimage fund board, Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). “We have already held engagement sessions with stakeholders.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The Meteorological Department has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states, with heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today. The alert covers districts in Perak (Manjung, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Muallim), Kelantan (Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang and Pasir Puteh), Terengganu (Kuala Nerus, Hulu Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu, Marang, Dungun and Kemaman), Pahang (Raub, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin), as well as Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The latest warning was issued at 3.45pm today.

items.title: [LIVE] Negri polls: BN now leading in 5 seats, PH leads in 4
items.summary: 5.34pm - Mambau - PH is leading with 74 votes. 5.36pm - Rahang - PH's Siau Meow Kong is leading with 25 votes. 5.49pm - Repah - BN's Koh Kim Swee is leading with 163 votes.

items.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing attacks Asean peace plan, sets out priorities
items.summary: NAYPYIDAW: Nearly four months after taking office, Myanmar's junta chief turned president Min Aung Hlaing on Friday criticised the regional Asean bloc's peace plan and outlined his government's plans for the war-torn Southeast Asian country. Myanmar was plunged into turmoil in February 2021 when the military ousted an elected government led by Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi, sparking protests that expanded into a protracted civil war, killing some 100,000 people and displacing millions. Following are some key points from his speech to parliament: Dismissing Asean's peace plan – known as the "Five Point Consensus" – Min Aung Hlaing said the 11-member bloc has discriminated against Myanmar.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 65.38pct as at 4pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 65.38 per cent as at 4pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 562,133 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Selangor Education Department offers support following Hulu Selangor teacher’s death, police probe ongoing
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 1 — The Selangor Education Department has deployed psychosocial support to a Hulu Selangor school after a teacher was found dead yesterday. In a statement, JPN Selangor said full cooperation was being given to police investigating the case. It added that priority was being placed on ensuring the victim’s family received the best possible assistance, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: DKU declares document dated April 19 unconstitutional
items.summary: He said the DKU meeting was attended by Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang of Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid; and Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, who fulfilled the requirements under Clause 20 of the UUTKNS 1959. "The Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong and Undang of Luak Jelebu were dismissed in accordance with the customary laws of their respective Luak on the applicable dates, while the purported Undang of Luak Rembau was never lawfully appointed under customary law as his appointment was not completed through the Istiadat Menzahirkan Kejadian Undang," he said in a statement here today. At the same meeting, the DKU also recognised that Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang of Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid were lawfully appointed according to the customary laws of their respective Luak.

items.title: South Korea asked Prabowo to open dialogue with North Korea
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto said on Friday that South Korean President Lee Jae Myung asked him whether he could visit North Korea to open dialogue, adding that he would go. As Prabowo spoke about Indonesia's pursuit of equally good relations with all countries, including China and The United States, he brought up the request made at his last visit to Seoul in April. "During my last visit to South Korea, their president asked me if I could visit North Korea to open some kind of a dialogue.

items.title: Tengku Permaisuri Selangor decries animal abuse, calls for stronger enforcement and harsher penalties
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 1 — Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin has voiced deep concern over continuing cases of cruelty towards pets and stray animals, particularly dogs and cats, which have recently gone viral. As Royal Patron of the Stray Free Selangor initiative under SPCA Selangor, Her Highness said acts of abuse, injury or killing not only contravene the law but also reflect society’s failure to uphold compassion and humanity. Her Highness said offenders must be investigated thoroughly and face appropriate legal action, including if the acts are committed by enforcement officers.

items.title: Sultan of Pahang: Public roads are not racetracks
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has urged the public to stop illegal street racing before more lives are lost, warning that such activities continue to endanger road users. "I am deeply saddened that some youths still choose public roads as a stage to seek fame, view the roar of engines as a symbol of bravery, and take pride in illegal street racing. Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.

items.title: Search continues for Nirmal Purja-led team after Pakistan avalanche
items.summary: SKARDU: Pakistan rescue teams resumed a high-altitude search on Saturday for seven climbers missing after a powerful avalanche on one of the world's highest peaks, with the remains of three mountaineers recovered. The avalanche struck Thursday, cutting off contact with the ten-member international expedition led by renowned British-Nepali climber Nirmal Purja – who is not among the remains recovered so far. Those recovered – flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification – included an American woman, an Omani woman, and a Nepali man, the regional government said in a statement released Friday night.

items.title: RCI report an opportunity to strengthen Tabung Haji, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) will not affect Malaysia's relationship with Saudi Arabia or its reputation for managing haj affairs. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the report should instead be viewed as an opportunity to further strengthen TH's management, governance and operations. He added that TH continued to receive international recognition for its haj management.

items.title: Strong Malaysia-Bahrain ties underpin historic Bahrain GP at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's selection to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix following the disruption to the 2026 Formula 1 championship calendar marks a landmark arrangement underpinned by a shared commitment to motorsport excellence and the close ties between the two countries. Bahrain's Ambassador to Malaysia, Dr Waleed Khalifa Al Manea, said the arrangement reflected the strong ties between the royal and political leadership of both countries. The arrangement reflects the strong ties between His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, which were further strengthened during the Malaysian King's state visit to Bahrain in 2025.

items.title: Sultan of Pahang: No compromise on illegal land encroachment
items.summary: KUANTAN: Every inch of the state's land must be protected from illegal encroachment and unlawful occupation, says the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. His Royal Highness said the law must be enforced without fear or favour, and without compromise, whenever the sovereignty of Pahang's land and the dignity of the state were at stake. Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.

items.title: Safar tour to allow contributors track wakaf progress firsthand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wakaf contributors will no longer have to rely solely on reports or updates to track the impact of their contributions, as the Federal Territories Waqf Safar Tour Programme will allow them to visit completed projects firsthand. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the programme would be held regularly to strengthen confidence among existing contributors while encouraging more people to participate in wakaf. "Insya-Allah, this programme will be held regularly and continuously to reassure existing contributors as well as potential contributors," he said at a press conference after launching the Federal Territories Waqf Safar Tour Programme Series 1 at the Darul Kifayah Complex in Batu Caves today.

items.title: EC: Over half of Negeri Sembilan voters turn out by 2pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1— As of 2 pm, 51.58 per cent, or 443,461 of the 859,760 registered voters, had cast their ballots in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. Based on a Facebook post by the Election Commission (EC), the Seri Menanti state constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 57.6 per cent, followed closely by Senaling at 57.2 per cent and Kota at 56.9 per cent. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 59.03pct as at 3pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 59.03 per cent as at 3 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 507,536 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Revive wakaf's golden era role beyond mosques and cemeteries
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said wakaf could play a bigger role in advancing education, healthcare, research and economic development. He said history showed that wakaf institutions were among the pillars of Islamic civilisation during its golden era in Baghdad, Andalusia and Istanbul. Zulkifli said strengthening the wakaf sector could reduce society's reliance on the government while fostering a more independent and empowered community.

items.title: Chief Justice heads Pahang honours list
items.summary: Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance. Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia. The Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri, was conferred on 16 people, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi and Dewan Rakyat deputy speaker Datuk Dr Ramli Mohd Nor, who is also the Cameron Highlands MP.

items.title: IGP says Sanusi case under investigation, police to obtain Kedah MB’s statement
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will record a statement from Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks he allegedly made touching on racial issues during a recent political ceramah in Jempol. According to Berita Harian , Inspector‑General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the case involving Sanusi remained under investigation. “This matter is still under investigation.

items.title: IGP: 92 reports received, 24 investigation papers opened pertaining to Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police received 92 reports and opened 24 investigation papers throughout the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, which ended at midnight last night. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said most of the reported offences involved minor cases linked to supporters or party members, while four reports on alleged cash handouts to voters were still under investigation. To date, there have been no police reports directly involving candidates, while the overall election process across the 36 state seats has proceeded smoothly and safely,” he said.

items.title: Perkep taps KJH to expand market for its products
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai has provided an ideal platform for the Police Family Association (Perkep) to expand the market reach of products produced by its entrepreneurs. Perkep chairman Puan Sri Munirah Che Rose said the association's maiden participation in the carnival enabled it to introduce a range of handmade products produced by wives of police officers and personnel. "KJH provides us with a valuable opportunity to introduce handmade products created by Perkep members, who are wives of police officers and personnel.

items.title: No repeat of Dataran Merdeka mess, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she did not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering. "Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish.

items.title: Bukit Aman awaits Indonesian details after Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta airport
items.summary: Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police are awaiting further details from their counterparts before determining the next course of action, the New Straits Times (NST) reported. Hussein told NST that investigators also wanted to determine how many times the suspect might have carried out similar operations and whether he was part of a wider network. Investigators are also examining how the suspect allegedly managed to pass through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 51.58pct as at 2pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 51.58 per cent as at 2 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 443,461 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Homecoming rush: Voters return, traffic builds across Negri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Traffic flow on several major routes around Seremban, as well as connecting roads to outlying districts such as Bukit Putus, Kuala Pilah and Kuala Klawang in Jelebu, has been reported to be steadily building since early this morning. Real-time traffic checks on Google Maps, Waze and Apple Maps revealed slow-moving traffic at several hotspots, particularly along the Seremban-Kuala Pilah road through Bukit Putus, the Seremban-Tampin route, and roads leading to Kuala Klawang in Jelebu. Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Supt Roslan Mohamed@Ab Aziz, when contacted, said conditions remained under control as of 2pm despite the noticeable increase in vehicles.

items.title: ‘Shared responsibility’: Hannah Yeoh urges public to help maintain cleanliness during Putrajaya National Day celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 1 — Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she does not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering. “Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish.

items.title: Tun Jugah-inspired hairstyle draws crowds at KJH Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak Tourism Board (STB) marketing administrative officer Ozie Tunggeng has been turning heads at the Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai with a distinctive hairstyle inspired by the legendary Iban leader, Tun Jugah anak Barieng. Throughout the carnival, Ozie has been promoting the state's tourism products and hosting interactive stage activities, including tourism quizzes. STB assistant marketing officer Nabil Aiman Sait said the board remains committed to promoting Sarawak's tourism offerings to both domestic and international visitors.

items.title: Mental health stigma leaves many suffering in silence, says Queen
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern that the stigma surrounding mental health continues to prevent many people from seeking professional help, leaving them to suffer in silence. Citing New Straits Times reports on the growing mental health crisis, Her Majesty said adults were increasingly burdened by financial hardship, debt and strained family relationships, often leading to severe psychological distress. Raja Zarith Sofiah, who received an Honorary Doctorate in Psychology from the university, said addressing the nation's mental health challenges had never been more important.

items.title: Police tighten security at Negeri Sembilan palace, state offices ahead of poll results
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will tighten security at key locations, including the Istana of the Yang di Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and state government offices, to prevent any untoward incidents when the Negeri Sembilan state election results are announced later tonight. Inspector General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said there was a possibility that certain quarters might attempt to stir tensions if dissatisfied with the outcome, Sinar Harian reported. Mohd Khalid was speaking to reporters after visiting the polling centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan King George V here today.

items.title: Chief Justice heads Pahang state honours list
items.summary: Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance. Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia.

items.title: Nerves, pride as 1st time voters cast their ballots
items.summary: SEREMBAN: For many first-time voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election today, casting their ballot was a memorable milestone marked by excitement, nerves and pride. Fashion designer Hani Eriqa Mazlan, 21, said voting for the first time gave her a deeper appreciation of the democratic process. "I was nervous and my hands were shaking because it was my first time voting.

items.title: CAP calls for tougher screening for pilots after Jakarta drug case
items.summary: CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the association was "shocked and disappointed" by the incident, calling it a major blow to Malaysia's aviation industry and public confidence in air travel. He said passenger safety must remain the highest priority, as travellers entrust their lives to pilots every time they board an aircraft. "Passengers expect pilots to be responsible for their lives on a flight.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 44.67pct as at 1pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 44.67 per cent as at 1 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 384,096 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Bukit Aman to work with Indonesian police in probe involving Malaysian pilot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman will work closely with their Indonesian counterparts in the investigation involving a Malaysian pilot arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs into the country. Bukit Aman Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan told the New Straits Times that police are awaiting more information from Indonesian authorities before determining the next course of action. Hussein said police are also studying the need to send a team of investigators to Indonesia to interview the suspect to establish the full circumstances surrounding the case.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan confirms two Undang appointments, declares three other claimants invalid
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has formally recognised two newly installed Undang and declared three individuals who claimed the titles of Undang Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu as never having held those positions lawfully. Muhammad Faris Johari was formerly recognised as the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, while Raja Hassan Ab Hamid’s appointment as Undang Luak Rembau was also affirmed under adat. The DKU also noted that the position of the position of Undang for Sungei Ujong is now vacant after the previous holder, Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, was removed according to adat effective 30 July 2026.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan election sees 37pc voter turnout by noon
items.summary: The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said the Juasseh constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 43.5 per cent, followed by Chennah (43.4 per cent) and Senaling (42.8 per cent). The Lukut constituency recorded the lowest turnout at about 32.1 per cent. For comparison, voter turnout at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election stood at 35.44 per cent, or 297,024 of the 838,200 registered voters.

items.title: Sisters steal the spotlight in Rantau, casting votes in Jalur Gemilang style ahead of Merdeka
items.summary: REMBAU, Aug 1 — In a vibrant display of national pride, two siblings turned heads at the polling centre in Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Chung Hua, Rantau today when they showed up dressed head-to-toe in Jalur Gemilang-themed attire, adding a festive splash to the occasion. Born and raised in Rantau, the duo decided to infuse their civic duty with the patriotic spirit of the upcoming National Day celebrations. Eldest sister Zamzarina Basiron, 45, explained that the idea came naturally.

items.title: Johor Bahru police seek e‑hailing driver to identify passenger accused of insulting Islam
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 1 — Police are tracking down an e-hailing driver to assist in the investigation and identify a suspect linked to a viral video containing remarks allegedly insulting Islam in Johor Bahru. Johor Bahru Selatan police chief ACP Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the district police headquarters received a report from a police officer at 3.25pm on July 31 after the officer came across the video on social media at about 2.30pm the same day. Anyone with information related to the incident is urged to contact the Johor Bahru Selatan Police Headquarters hotline at 07-2182323 or report the matter at the nearest police station.

items.title: Civil servants swap desks for hybrid rhythm as SPOT‑Me tracks Malaysia’s new workday experiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy comes into force today, allowing civil servants to work three days in the office and two days from home or alternative locations. The Public Service Department (JPA) described the implementation of the HBH Policy as a future-proof measure to ensure government service delivery remains resilient amid global changes and the evolution of modern working methods, without compromising the quality of services provided to the people. Under the HBH Implementation Guidelines, states observing Sunday as the weekly holiday will have Monday and Friday designated as compulsory office attendance days.

items.title: Licensed hunter urges cooperation as Sibu crocodile chase draws roadside crowds, sparks traffic chaos
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 1 — Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew has appealed for public cooperation after roadside crowds gathered along Jalan Oya–Sibu Jaya during a crocodile capture operation on Thursday evening, causing traffic congestion and raising safety concerns. Siew said many motorists stopped and parked along the roadside to watch the operation, disrupting traffic flow along the busy stretch of road. Jeferry Siew and his team in action, trying to capture the elusive crocodile.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls see 28.11pc turnout by 11am, says EC
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voter turnout in the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election stood at 28.11 per cent as of 11am today, according to Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. He said observations at several polling centres around Seremban showed encouraging participation in the morning, with senior citizens making up a larger number of voters compared to younger voters. “We want to assess the system across different groups of voters, including senior citizens and younger voters.

items.title: Teacher clings to life in Pasir Mas well as firefighters stage dramatic morning rescue
items.summary: The woman, a teacher at a secondary school near Pasir Mas, lost her footing and plunged into the 5.48-meter-deep well, located behind her kitchen at approximately 7.50am. The Pasir Mas Fire and Rescue Department received the distress call and deployed a team of six firefighters, led by senior fire officer I Asraf Mat Naizi, who arrived at the scene just six minutes later. The woman was carefully hoisted out of the narrow well, and luckily suffered only minor injuries.

items.title: Election Commission chief Ramlan Harun inspects Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today visited three polling centres in Seremban to monitor the voting process and ensure the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election is proceeding smoothly and in an orderly manner. Ramlan then visited Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Haji Mohd Said, also in the Sikamat constituency, before concluding his tour at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato’ Klana Petra Maamor, which serves the Ampangan state constituency. During the visits, he received briefings from election officials on the voting process and inspected the facilities provided for voters and election personnel.

items.title: Police probe dog’s death during stray capture operation in Port Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 1 — Police have opened an investigation paper into the death of a dog during a stray dog capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, three days ago, following allegations of animal cruelty. South Klang police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the dog was confirmed dead after the incident, which occurred at about 10.50 pm on July 29 in front of a house in the residential area. He said the operation was carried out by the Royal Klang City Council (MBDK) with the cooperation of residents.

items.title: HKL refutes viral video claims of filthy toilets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) has denied claims that its public toilets are dirty and poorly maintained, as alleged in a video that went viral on Facebook yesterday. In a statement today, HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K. R. Nair said the hospital management had taken note of the allegations and conducted a thorough investigation. “The investigation into all public toilet facilities under HKL’s management found that the toilet shown in the viral video is not located within any facility under HKL’s supervision.

items.title: Siblings lose mother, youngest brother in Gua Musang crash a year after father's death
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Aug 1 — Exactly one year after losing their father, three siblings have been dealt another devastating blow with the deaths of their mother and youngest sibling in a road accident along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road near Gua Sejuk here yesterday. Their uncle, Mohamad Faizol Yusoff, 34, said his sister, Maria Yusoff, 42, had been raising her four children, aged between 11 and 21, on her own after her husband died of illness last year. Mohamad Faizol also said he and his siblings would take care of Maria’s children.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan caretaker MB Aminuddin casts ballot, says Pakatan confident despite predictions
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voting began this morning in the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, with caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun saying Pakatan Harapan (PH) remained unfazed by forecasts and external analyses. Aminuddin added that PH was not affected by outside speculation and expressed confidence the coalition could secure more than 19 seats. In Linggi, he faces a three-cornered contest against Barisan Nasional incumbent Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Bersatu’s Datuk Zamri Md Said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan state election: Early voter turnout at 8.29pc by 9am
items.summary: The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said Labu recorded the highest turnout so far at 10.4 per cent, followed by Senaling (10.3 per cent) and Ampangan (9.4 per cent). Rantau recorded the lowest turnout at 6.4 per cent. For comparison, the voter turnout recorded at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan State Election was 9.49 per cent, involving 79,557 out of 838,200 registered voters.
